critique: Both frames show a small, soft-edged orange circular blob. It has only a slight rightward displacement from 0.01 to 0.08 seconds, but no readable explosive particle separation, directional flame shape, bright yellow-white core, or sharp transient burst characteristic of the Muzzle Flash 1 (Explosive) thumbnail. The 150000/sec burst creates so much overlapping material that the particles merge into a uniform puff.

suggestions.why: Reduce the burst density so individual fast particles can resolve as an explosive flash rather than blending into one opaque round cloud.
Restore punch and a luminous flash after reducing particle count; the current 30% particle opacity produces a dull orange result.
Shift the particle body toward the hotter yellow-orange expected of a muzzle-flash core instead of the current uniformly deep orange.
